chapterName: Chapter 1 – Introduction to Business Process Configuration

questions.question: What does configuring an ERP system primarily involve?

options.A: Selecting the desired options and specifying parameters so that processes run as the organization wants
options.B: Rewriting the delivered program code to add new capabilities to the software
options.C: Training the end users of the organization to operate the new ERP system
options.D: Moving every legacy record into the new system without reviewing the data

questions.explanation: Configuration is a matter of selecting options and specifying parameters (boundaries for data values); it is not changing code.

questions.question: Which activity involves adding new code or modifying existing code of the delivered ERP software?
questions.explanation: Customization changes the delivered software by adding or modifying programming code.

questions.question: How does the text define implementation of an ERP system?

options.A: Selecting the capabilities to include, setting up the system, and training the users
options.B: Changing the underlying programming code of the ERP system to fit the company
options.C: Creating only the enterprise structure and master data of the organization
options.D: Executing test transactions to validate that the system behaves as designed

questions.explanation: Implementation covers choosing capabilities, system setup and training; configuration is only one part of it.

questions.question: How many phases does the standard ASAP (Accelerated SAP) methodology consist of?
questions.explanation: ASAP phases: project preparation, business blueprint, realization, final preparation, go-live, operation.

questions.question: In which ASAP phase is the business blueprint applied to the ERP system (configuration is performed)?
questions.explanation: Configuration is a component of the realization phase.

questions.question: Which ASAP phase documents the organization's business process requirements?
questions.explanation: The business blueprint phase creates a common understanding of the processes to implement and documents requirements.

questions.question: Testing, end-user training and cutting over from the old system happen in which ASAP phase?
questions.explanation: Final preparation follows configuration/customization and includes testing, training, system management and cutover.

questions.question: What is the focus of the ASAP "Operation" phase?

options.A: Managing the new system so the supported business processes keep performing
options.B: Creating the initial planning for the implementation project
options.C: Applying the business blueprint to the ERP system
options.D: Moving the users from the old system to the new system

questions.explanation: After go-live, the focus turns to managing operation of the system.

questions.question: Which two customization options does the text describe?
questions.explanation: Modification changes underlying code; enhancement adds capabilities without changing it.

questions.question: Which customization option requires knowledge of SAP's proprietary programming language ABAP?
questions.explanation: Modification changes the existing underlying code, which is written in ABAP.

questions.question: Why are enhancements preferred over modifications?

options.A: They are always cheaper to build than any configuration option in the system
options.B: They allow the vendor to replace all of the underlying code of the ERP system
options.C: The standard programming code is left unchanged, which avoids problems when the software is upgraded
options.D: They remove the need for any testing after the system has been changed

questions.explanation: Modified code may conflict with new vendor code during an upgrade.

questions.question: What is a user exit?

options.A: An identified location in the program code where the ERP system connects to an external program or system
options.B: A setting that logs a user out of the system after a period of inactivity
options.C: A master data record describing how an employee leaves the company
options.D: A document that records the movement of materials in the system

questions.explanation: At a user exit the ERP passes data to the external system, waits for the results, then continues.

questions.question: An organization requires manager approval for purchase orders over $5,000. How is this practice set up in the ERP system?

options.A: By modifying the ABAP code of the purchase order transaction for the company
options.B: By creating a new company code that handles only high-value purchases
options.C: By selecting the approval option and specifying $5,000 as the parameter that triggers approval
options.D: By defining a customer master record with the $5,000 approval limit

questions.explanation: Configuration = choose the option (approval) and the parameter value ($5,000).

topics.topicName: Four types of data & enterprise structure

questions.question: How many types of data are there in an ERP system according to the text?
questions.explanation: Enterprise structure, business rules and parameters, master data, and transaction data.

questions.question: Which type of data is the most common in an ERP system?
questions.explanation: Transaction data reflect the impacts of executing process steps and are created constantly.

questions.question: Which type of data reflects the consequences of executing the organization's business practices?
questions.explanation: The first three types represent the physical environment; transaction data reflect the consequences of executing practices.

questions.question: Enterprise structure data are also known as:
questions.explanation: Enterprise structure represents the legal, functional and business-focused components of the enterprise.

questions.question: Which enterprise structure element represents the whole enterprise?
questions.explanation: The highest level in the GBI structure figure is the client.

questions.question: How is each legal company represented in the ERP enterprise structure?
questions.explanation: GBI has two companies (U.S. and Germany), each represented by a company code.

questions.question: Which enterprise structure element represents a facility where materials are manufactured or stored?
questions.explanation: Factories and distribution centers are represented by plants.

questions.question: What do business rules represent in an ERP system?

options.A: The organization's business practices, which determine how process steps are executed
options.B: The legal and functional structure of the organization in the system
options.C: The core data about customers, vendors and materials of the company
options.D: The records created when a process step has been completed

questions.explanation: Business rules, e.g. manager approval above a threshold, are configured to reflect practices.

questions.question: What are parameters in an ERP system?

options.A: Electronic records of the consequences of process steps
options.B: Names and addresses of customers and vendors
options.C: Boundaries for data that influence how processes are executed in the system
options.D: Organizational units such as plants and company codes

questions.explanation: Parameters are closely related to business rules; defaults can be changed during configuration.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a business rule?

options.A: Allowing partial deliveries from a vendor within configured limits
options.B: The name and address of a vendor
options.C: The date a sales order was created
options.D: The company code of the German company

questions.explanation: Whether under/over or partial deliveries are accepted is configured as a business rule.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a parameter?

options.A: The number and description of a general ledger account
options.B: The quantity entered on a sales order by the salesperson
options.C: The specifications that determine how many bicycles each factory can produce
options.D: The weight of a material stored in the material master

questions.explanation: Parameters are boundaries for data, e.g., production limits or availability-check settings.

questions.question: What are master data?

options.A: Data typed in by the user when a transaction is created
options.B: Organizational elements that represent the structure of the company
options.C: Boundaries for data that influence how a process step runs
options.D: The core data of an organization and its business processes

questions.explanation: Master data describe relationships with customers and vendors, treatment of materials and the financial accounts.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of master data?

options.A: The requested delivery date on a sales order
options.C: The order type selected for a sales order
options.D: The quantity ordered by a customer

questions.explanation: Name/address of customers and vendors, material weight and G/L account descriptions are master data.

questions.question: At which level are general master data maintained?

options.A: The plant level only, separately for every factory
options.B: The company code level only, separately for every company
options.C: The sales area level only, separately for every region
options.D: The client level, applicable to all company codes and plants

questions.explanation: General data are client-level; financial accounting data align with company code; process data with process-specific elements.

questions.question: Financial accounting master data are most closely aligned with which enterprise structure element?
questions.explanation: Financial accounting data are defined for the company code.

questions.question: Why must master data of the same vendor be defined separately for each company code?

options.A: Because a vendor can only be created once for each plant in the system
options.B: Because the client level does not allow any vendor data to be stored
options.C: Each company may have a different relationship with the vendor, such as different payment terms
options.D: Because payment terms are always identical for all companies of the client

questions.explanation: GBI U.S. and GBI Germany may buy from the same vendor under different terms.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a master data-cleaning project during configuration?

options.A: To correct or remove inaccurate data and eliminate redundant data before it enters the new system
options.B: To convert all master data into transaction data in the new system
options.C: To replace the new numbering scheme with the numbers of the legacy system
options.D: To customize the ERP software so it accepts any type of legacy data

questions.explanation: Only current, accurate, high-quality master data should be moved from the legacy system.

questions.question: Which material type is purchased from a vendor and used in production but normally not sold to customers?
questions.explanation: Raw-material master data include purchasing data but not sales data (unless sold as spare parts).

questions.question: Which material type is procured from a vendor and sold to customers with no additional value added?
questions.explanation: Water bottles at GBI are trading goods; their master data include purchasing and selling data, not production data.

questions.question: Which material type is made from raw materials and semifinished goods and is sold to customers?
questions.explanation: Finished products (e.g., bicycles) are produced and sold.

questions.question: Which material type is produced in-house and used to make finished products, but is neither purchased nor sold?
questions.explanation: A wheel assembly is an example of a semifinished good.

questions.question: What does a bill of materials (BOM) identify?

options.A: The operations or activities needed to make a material
options.B: The physical location where production operations take place
options.C: The components needed to make a material
options.D: The number of products a work center can produce per period

questions.explanation: BOM = components; routing = operations; work center = location; capacity = output over time.

questions.question: What does a routing identify?

options.A: The operations or activities needed to make a material
options.B: The components needed to make a material
options.C: The financial accounts used when a material is produced
options.D: The vendors from which a material can be purchased

questions.explanation: Routing lists the operations; they are carried out in a work center.

questions.question: What is a work center?

options.A: A list of components required to produce a material
options.B: A document that records the movement of materials
options.C: A physical location where production operations take place
options.D: An organizational element that represents a legal company

questions.explanation: Work centers have the capacity to execute certain types of operations.

questions.question: What does capacity of a work center describe?

options.A: The maximum value of purchase orders that the work center may approve
options.B: The number of products the work center can produce in a specified amount of time with its resources
options.C: The number of operations contained in the routing of a material
options.D: The amount of storage space available for finished products

questions.explanation: Capacity is broadly categorized as labor capacity and machine capacity.

questions.question: Which three types of data do vendor and customer master records include?

options.A: Enterprise structure, parameters, and situational data
options.B: Unit, scenario, and integration testing data
options.D: General data, data defining the terms of the relationship, and data to record the financial consequences

questions.explanation: E.g. account number/name/address, payment terms, and reconciliation-account information.

questions.question: Of which data are transaction data comprised?

options.A: Only the data entered by the user when the transaction is saved
options.B: Only business rules and parameters configured by the project team
options.C: Enterprise structure data, master data, and situational data (influenced by rules and parameters)
options.D: Only the data imported from the legacy system during master data cleaning

questions.explanation: Situational data are typically input by the user: who, what, when, where.

questions.question: Which of the following is situational data on a sales order?

options.A: The quantity ordered and the requested delivery date
options.B: The company code and the sales area
options.C: The customer's payment terms stored in the customer master
options.D: The availability check configured for the order type

questions.explanation: Date, time, location and quantity are examples of situational data entered by the user.

questions.question: Which document records the consequences of a process step on the general ledger?
questions.explanation: FI document = G/L; CO document = management accounting; MM document = movement of materials.

questions.question: Which document records the movement of materials?
questions.explanation: MM documents maintain a record of material movements.

questions.question: In which order must the data be configured?

options.A: Master data, then enterprise structure, then business rules and parameters, then testing
options.B: Enterprise structure, then business rules and parameters, then master data, then testing
options.C: Business rules and parameters, then master data, then enterprise structure, then testing
options.D: Testing, then enterprise structure, then master data, then business rules and parameters

questions.explanation: Master data cannot be added until enterprise structure and related rules/parameters are configured.

questions.question: What are the two primary test types for ERP system testing?

options.B: Regression testing and user acceptance testing

questions.explanation: Functional testing checks behavior; performance testing checks the system handles expected volumes efficiently.

questions.question: What is the purpose of performance (load) testing?

options.A: To ensure the system behaves as desired for each business process
options.B: To assess usability close to go-live by giving users a feel for the system
options.C: To ensure the system can accommodate the expected volume of transactions efficiently
options.D: To verify that changes did not affect processes that were not modified

questions.explanation: Only functional testing is discussed in the book.

questions.question: Which functional test is the lowest level and executes each individual transaction (process step)?
questions.explanation: Unit testing ensures that each process step functions as expected.

questions.question: Which functional test focuses on the interaction of multiple related transactions, including tests that are expected to fail?
questions.explanation: Some scenarios use erroneous input; failure to detect errors also indicates incorrect configuration.

questions.question: Which functional test checks end-to-end business processes, possibly across several systems and non-SAP interfaces?
questions.explanation: Integration testing involves significant cross-process (and possibly cross-system) testing.

questions.question: Which functional test is usually performed close to go-live to assess usability?
questions.explanation: It is often embedded in new-user training to give users a feel for the new system.

questions.question: When is regression testing performed?

options.A: Only once, immediately after the enterprise structure has been configured
options.B: Only after go-live, when the users first sign in to the new system
options.C: During system changes such as enhancement packages, configuration modifications or significant master data changes
options.D: Only when the organization chooses to customize the ERP system

questions.explanation: It also tests processes that are not impacted to make sure they were not changed inadvertently.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the five core processes the book focuses on?
questions.explanation: The five: financial accounting, management accounting, procurement, fulfillment, production.

questions.question: Which chapter and process correspond to the "procure to pay" process?
questions.explanation: Procurement is often called "procure to pay"; fulfillment is "order to cash".

questions.question: Which process is often called "order to cash"?
questions.explanation: Fulfillment is concerned with selling products and services to customers.

questions.question: Financial accounting is mainly focused on meeting the reporting requirements of whom?

options.A: Internal managers who control costs and revenues
options.B: The plant supervisors of each factory
options.C: The customers who order the products
options.D: External entities such as regulators and shareholders

questions.explanation: Management accounting is internally focused (cost/revenue management).
